title: A Legion Wearing One Face
subtitle: Nova Nyarindo Newbon Gadson's archetypal theory of the person, meeting, myth, and reality
author: Nova Nyarindo Newbon Gadson
workingPrinciple: A person is a legion of archetypes, with one convinced it is the whole at any given time.
disclaimer: Everyone shown, including religious figures, public figures, fictional characters, institutions, and the author, is used as an archetype. The images use what is known to communicate what cannot be fully known. Inclusion is symbolic, not a factual claim about any person, a declaration on behalf of any tradition, or an endorsement of any system.

works.title: The Person You Meet
works.caption: The visible face before the archetypal council is named.
works.alt: A full-length stylized portrait of Nova Nyarindo Newbon Gadson smiling barefoot on green grass beneath a broad tree.
works.description: The portrait is the first layer: one visible person standing in the world. It deliberately does not reveal the many roles, memories, needs, and perspectives working beneath the face.

works.title: The Legion Beneath
works.caption: Twelve common human roles that may take charge at different times.
works.alt: A twelve-part illustrated chart of Hero, Lover, Creator, Sage, Innocent, Explorer, Ruler, Caregiver, Jester, Rebel, Magician, and Everyman archetypes.
works.description: The chart makes the inner cast visible. These roles are tools for noticing recurring patterns, not permanent personality labels or diagnoses.

works.title: The Meeting
works.caption: Two people meet, and the room fills with the voices through which they meet themselves.
works.alt: A crowded cartoon council around a table, with Sage, Judge, Defender, Lover, Skeptic, Believer, Questioner, Philosopher, Observer, Fool, Trickster, Peacemaker, and Child archetypes in conversation.
works.description: The first meeting is ordinary. Two people could be anyone, and one could be the viewer. Their inner roles disagree, joke, defend, question, care, and call one another back.

works.title: The Spiral Called a Meeting
works.caption: The human meeting expands into the scale of myth.
works.alt: A mythic council beneath sun and moon, gathering human archetypes, God the Father, Yeshua, Lilith, the Observer, the Child, and animal companions around one table.
works.description: The same meeting now includes divine figures, mythic figures, ancestors, humans, animals, celestial bodies, and symbols. The ordinary encounter is not replaced by myth; it is seen more widely through myth.

works.title: The Final Act
works.caption: Every map and authority enters, while Wonder remains on the throne.
works.alt: A panoramic satirical collage of religious figures, public figures, institutions, worldviews, and archetypes gathered around the Child of Wonder on a throne of faith, knowledge, wisdom, and proof.
works.description: Religions, philosophies, nations, institutions, economies, technologies, celebrities, fictional characters, and archetypes all arrive carrying partial maps. The Child of Wonder sits at the centre, guarded by experienced fools and tricksters.

characters.depictedAction: Appears as the visible person in the opening portrait and as a reminder that the two people in the meeting could be anyone.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The author is also part of the theory. No one stands outside the archetypal process.

characters.depictedAction: Faces challenge and tries to create change.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that moves toward difficulty when courage feels necessary.

characters.depictedAction: Builds connection and feels deeply.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part oriented toward intimacy, attachment, beauty, and union.

characters.depictedAction: Brings imagination into form.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that makes something new from attention, material, and possibility.

characters.depictedAction: Consults books and attempts to clarify what is known.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that seeks truth and shares wisdom, while also risking detachment from lived experience.

characters.depictedAction: Finds joy and looks for the good.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that preserves hope, simplicity, and the possibility of renewal.

characters.depictedAction: Looks toward the horizon and seeks freedom through discovery.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that tests the boundary of the familiar and wants to know what lies beyond it.

characters.depictedAction: Creates order and leads with confidence.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that seeks structure, responsibility, and control.

characters.depictedAction: Nurtures, supports, and lifts others.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part organised around protection, generosity, and relational responsibility.

characters.depictedAction: Brings play, laughter, and surprise into serious situations.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that loosens certainty and can reach truths that solemnity cannot.

characters.depictedAction: Questions the norm and resists unjust constraint.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that refuses a premise or authority when obedience would cost integrity.

characters.depictedAction: Works with hidden laws, transformation, and possibility.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that perceives pattern, change, and unseen relation, while risking manipulation.

characters.depictedAction: Connects, belongs, and keeps things real.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The ordinary, relational self through whom every other role must ultimately live.

characters.depictedAction: Calls objection and evaluates the rules of the meeting.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that judges truth, fairness, and procedure, but can mistake judgment for the whole person.

characters.depictedAction: Guards the boundary and asks who is approaching.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The protective part that keeps the self safe, but can mistake every difference for an attack.

characters.depictedAction: Demands evidence and tests the claims on the table.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that protects against credulity and asks belief to answer to reality.

characters.depictedAction: Holds trust even while evidence remains incomplete.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that commits, relates, and remains faithful without claiming to possess proof of everything.

characters.depictedAction: Interrupts certainty with a question about how the group knows.
dialogue: Interesting... but how do we know that?
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that keeps inquiry alive and prevents inherited assumptions from becoming invisible.

characters.depictedAction: Distinguishes concepts, analyses language, and reconsiders the premise.
dialogue: Let us distinguish: consider, analyse, contextualise, perhaps reframe the premise.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that examines the structure of a question before accepting its terms.

characters.depictedAction: Watches the meeting and notices its patterns without immediately taking a side.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The witnessing awareness that can see the whole pattern before identifying with one voice.

characters.depictedAction: Questions the frame, introduces reversal, and protects play.
dialogue: What if both of you are wrong?
characters.symbolicMeaning: The experienced fool who can unsettle false certainty and guard Wonder from capture.

characters.depictedAction: Tries to lower the temperature and keep the meeting survivable.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The part that protects relationship and continuity, while risking avoidance of necessary conflict.

characters.depictedAction: Sits at or near the centre of the meeting and calls everyone back with the word Again.
characters.symbolicMeaning: Openness before certainty hardens. Wonder is not ignorance; it is the living centre that every system must protect.

characters.depictedAction: Appears as a crowned elder on the council's elevated left side.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic image of origin, sovereignty, law, and the ancestral authority that the meeting must encounter.

characters.depictedAction: Appears among the central mythic figures and again in the final archetype band.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic figure of embodied peace, teaching, and authority held alongside human voices rather than above the meeting's questions.

characters.depictedAction: Appears in the mythic council and in the final archetype band as a distinct iconographic portrayal.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic figure of love, sacrifice, and pastoral care within the work's plural mythic language.

characters.depictedAction: Appears crowned in firelight on the elevated right side of the mythic council.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A mythic figure of autonomy, creation, desire, fire, and maternal power.

characters.depictedAction: Appears beside the serpent and fruit in the final panorama.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic figure of beginning, choice, knowledge, and the cost of entering a larger world.

characters.depictedAction: Stands beside Yeshua in the mythic assembly and final panorama.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A witness figure of devotion, insight, grief, and fidelity to what was seen.

characters.depictedAction: Appears in the mythic assembly and the final archetype band.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A figure of rupture, exclusion, costly choice, and the unanswered question of belonging.

characters.depictedAction: Appears crowned among the mythic authorities, associated with a constructed order.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic figure of the world-building power that mistakes its map for the whole of reality.

characters.depictedAction: Appears as a horned mythic authority and again as The Rebel in the archetype band.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbol of refusal, illumination, pride, and the danger and necessity of rebellion.

characters.depictedAction: Appears with writing and sacred knowledge in the final panorama.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic figure of writing, measurement, magic, and the ordering of knowledge.

characters.depictedAction: Sits serenely amid the competing authorities.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbol of awakening, release from fixation, and disciplined attention.

characters.depictedAction: Appears beside Buddha as a figure of ancient wisdom.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbol of natural order, non-forcing, and wisdom that moves with the way of things.

characters.depictedAction: Appears beside the assembled sacred and mythic authorities in the final panorama.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbol of irrepressible intelligence, disruption, courage, and the refusal of imposed limits.

characters.depictedAction: Coils beside Eve and the fruit in the final panorama.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbol of prohibited knowledge, temptation, transformation, and the awakening of choice.

characters.depictedAction: Appears as a radiant human-faced sun in the upper-left sky.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The ordering source of visible life, certainty, and illumination.

characters.depictedAction: Appears in the night sky as a face within the moon.
characters.symbolicMeaning: The rhythm of shadow, reflection, and knowledge received indirectly.

characters.depictedAction: Appears as a small flat world at the lower left, saying that something is standing on it.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbol of a map being mistaken for the whole of the terrain.

characters.depictedAction: Appears as a small globe nearby, answering the Flat Earth personification.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbol that a larger model may hold more of reality without becoming reality itself.

characters.depictedAction: Appears at the left edge among liberation voices.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic public persona associated with freedom, resistance, and collective spirit.

characters.depictedAction: Appears as a musical and cultural voice in the Kenyan cluster.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic public persona representing expressive local identity and lived experience.

characters.depictedAction: Appears as a musical and cultural voice in the Kenyan cluster.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic public persona representing storytelling, memory, and popular cultural knowledge.

characters.depictedAction: Sits near the central court and appears in the archetype strip as The Fool.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbol of knowing self-awareness and humour that can puncture false authority.

characters.depictedAction: Sits beside the Child and destabilises the court's seriousness.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbol of chaos that exposes how fragile order can be and how laughter can become a weapon.

characters.depictedAction: Appears among the cultural caricatures to the right of the throne.

characters.depictedAction: Appears among the celebrated public figures to the right of the throne.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic persona of excellence, competition, influence, and the public hero.

characters.depictedAction: Appears among the global pop-culture figures.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic persona of spectacle, transformation, and the enormous reach of performance.

characters.depictedAction: Appears among the action-cinema caricatures.

characters.depictedAction: Appears at the far right with a rocket labelled Peace.

characters.depictedAction: Appears beside China in the central power row.

characters.depictedAction: Appears as a masked legal enforcer among the global powers.

characters.depictedAction: Appears on the lower right with the words Origins, Resilience, Future.

characters.depictedAction: Appears beside Africa with the words Stories, People, Possibilities.

characters.depictedAction: Appear at the lower right with the words Journey, Identity, Return.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbol of inherited journey, contested identity, and the call to return.

characters.depictedAction: Appears in the final archetype band as the Sage.
characters.symbolicMeaning: Wisdom personified as the seeker of truth and sharer of knowledge.

characters.depictedAction: Appears in the final archetype band as the Hero.
characters.symbolicMeaning: Strength and courage as a gift inseparable from vulnerability.

characters.depictedAction: Appears as a central musical celebrity beneath the title of the Final Act.

characters.depictedAction: Appears at the far right beside the cultural and political figures.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic figure of the shadow that haunts order from its edge.

characters.depictedAction: Appears in a lab coat among the caricatures, associated with the speech bubble Science, bro!

characters.depictedAction: Appears beside Rick Sanchez amid the Final Act caricatures.

characters.depictedAction: Appears on the left as people carry a flag and a We Remember sign.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic map of memory, belonging, and inheritance.

characters.depictedAction: Appears on the left as people carry a flag and a We Endure sign.
characters.symbolicMeaning: A symbolic map of endurance, grief, and survival.

characters.depictedAction: Appears near the glowing centre beneath the line Truth Still Showed Up.
characters.symbolicMeaning: Reality's presence within the unfinished argument, never reduced to any one speaker.

messages.text: The map is not the terrain, but it can help us travel.
messages.meaning: Models are partial tools, never the whole of reality.

messages.text: Not a circle of repetition, but a return with something new.
messages.meaning: The spiral is growth through return, not repetition for its own sake.

messages.text: Observe. Question. Learn. Participate. Begin again.
messages.meaning: The sequence of the spiral as a lived practice.

messages.text: A question. A laugh. A kinder listen. A clearer see. A fuller life. Again.
messages.meaning: The meeting becomes a fuller life through inquiry, humility, humour, and return.

messages.text: The world does not stop being a mystery when we stop explaining it.
messages.meaning: Explanation must not mistake itself for exhaustive knowledge.

messages.text: Different voices. A wider understanding. A kinder world.
messages.meaning: The purpose of plurality is wider understanding, not victory for one voice.

messages.text: The truce keeps the meeting open.
messages.meaning: Coexistence preserves the possibility of further learning.
Reality keeps moving and calls the council into another return.

messages.text: Everyone pointed. Everyone knew. No one knew. Truth still showed up.
messages.meaning: Every perspective carries certainty and partial blindness, yet reality remains present to the process.

messages.text: Same soil. Same people. Same story. Different maps.
messages.meaning: Shared human ground is often divided by competing maps and inherited stories.
Inquiry and measurement are both useful maps, and both can become ideologies when absolutised.
Four ways of relating to certainty surround Wonder without replacing it.
Reality remains present even when every participant holds only a partial map.
Competing perspectives can provoke a search for a larger truth without becoming identical.
A public declaration of exclusive reverence, included as one voice within the crowded field of belief.
A colloquial question in the crowd, kept as part of the lived, unfinished conversation.
A call of resistance using Babylon as a symbol of oppressive power.
Memory and endurance speak from two sides of a shared, unresolved history.

messages.text: I'm flat! / You're standing on me!
messages.meaning: The image makes rival models comic without letting either map disappear.
Scientific identity enters the argument as a cultural stance, not only a method.
Every viewpoint can claim a wider picture while still remaining a viewpoint.
Money and finance present themselves as world-moving forces.
A reminder that even confident systems do not possess the whole.

messages.text: We argued about the map, while forgetting the journey.
messages.meaning: The argument over representation can obscure lived reality itself.

messages.text: The end? Or a better beginning... You decide.
messages.meaning: The work ends by returning responsibility to the participant.
